rationale: Interpreting the sweep and extending the trim probe. (1) CheckRun 398a42387e1742c3b3f7cbfbbc0b75d4 (exit 0, all seven cases passed) evaluated every comparison of the tick-period sweep completely, so I append the current account of the runtime question on that self-contained receipt: the control at 2 ms holds, the partition at 2 and 4 ms holds (documented Superseded arm), and the partition at 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms is violated with valid witnesses - i.e. with the ~2 ms re-synchronisation round trip of this harness the false success appears once the tick period reaches 8 ms, which includes the crate's own default tick period of 10 ms. That replaces the previous two-point characterisation and its limitation, and I promote the bound to knowledge. (2) Locally I extended the trim probe with the generalised trigger and the result matched the source-derived expectation: ids {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3} both keep the compacted index at 0 with `trim(None)` returning ok and `trim(Some(1))` returning NotAllDecided(0), so the trigger is measured as 'largest node id exceeds the node count' rather than only the probed {1,2,5}. I submit that extended probe so the generalisation rests on a receipt instead of on the sizing code alone.

investigations.discriminator: The tick band is now measured; what remains is only the follower-origin variant (index arriving through the leader's `Assigned` reply), which shares this cause and responsibility and would not change the defect account, plus any callers outside this repository that treat the resolution as a durability signal.

The extended probe submitted here should confirm the generalised trigger (largest id above node count) on a receipt; after that only untested variants remain - ids that are contiguous but start above 1 in a larger cluster, and the behaviour after a snapshot has already compacted part of the log.

knowledge.statement: The false `append_notify` success is the ordinary outcome once the actor tick period exceeds the re-synchronisation round trip. Measured on the same lost-entry scenario with a ~2 ms round trip (1 ms egress each way): the documented `Superseded` arm was delivered at tick periods of 2 ms and 4 ms, and the false success - `resolved` = ok while the decided entry at the returned index was the new leader's entry and the caller's entry was in no decided log - at 8 ms, 16 ms, 40 ms and 80 ms. The crate's own `RuntimeConfig::default()` uses a 10 ms tick period with a 1 ms egress period, so the default configuration lies inside the band where the false success is expected for this interleaving.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, majority quorum, batch_size 1, in-process in-memory transport with whole-message drops, node 1 the pre-partition leader, entry 11 accepted only locally, new leader deciding entry 22 at the same index, origin re-synchronized in-process. Numbers hold for this round trip; the band scales with the re-synchronisation round trip, which was not varied (egress stayed at 1 ms).

interpretations.rationale: Current account on a self-contained receipt. `append_notify` assignments carry only `(log index, ballot at assignment)`; `drain_notifiers`, reachable only from the actor's tick branch, answers `Ok(assigned_idx)` as soon as `assigned_idx <= local decided index` and evaluates the ballot-change arm only afterwards, never comparing the caller's entry with what occupies that index. The tick-period sweep evaluates all seven declared predicates on real actor instances with a ~2 ms re-synchronisation round trip: the no-partition control at 2 ms holds (entry 11 decided at the returned index), the partition at 2 ms and at 4 ms holds (the documented `Superseded` arm is delivered, origin decided index 0 at resolution, entry 11 in no decided log), and the partition at 8 ms, 16 ms, 40 ms and 80 ms is violated with valid witnesses (index 17, 21, 25 for the new points and 9 for 80 ms): each resolved `ok` with assigned index 1 while the decided entry at index 1 was the new leader's entry 22 and the origin's decided log held only 22 - the origin's own entry is in no decided log anywhere. So the false completion is not an edge case of one tick setting: it is what the caller receives whenever the tick period exceeds the re-synchronisation round trip, and the crate's own `RuntimeConfig::default()` tick period is 10 ms with a 1 ms egress period, which lies inside that band. The caller-facing consequence is sourced in this repository: the async example documents `append_notify` as synchronous durability confirmation for a specific entry 'decided at its assigned index' and prints 'durably decided at log idx {idx}, safe to announce' without re-reading the log there, while the existing runtime test asserts only a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix. Scope: this actor layer, whole-message-loss with election-timeout takeover, batch_size 1, majority quorum, in-process in-memory transport. Earlier receipts of the same question (3fea35115a164e10bd378355a297b42f, fc17700defb243bfad08ed6717fb32fd, 420bbfc415a14e20ad9a6689d1775917) are retained in history and show the same two arms with the same setup.
counterevidence: The entry-point documentation promises only that the future resolves "when the assigned log index is decided", and for Superseded advises re-reading the returned index; read that way `Ok(idx)` is a claim about the index and not about the caller's value, so a caller that verifies the entry at the returned index is not misled. This weakens the caller-facing consequence but not the schedule dependence, since one lost-entry state cannot legitimately yield both `Superseded` and `Ok` if the signal describes state rather than timing.

A new leader must adopt any value a majority-overlapping write quorum already accepted, so an entry that reached a write quorum cannot be replaced; the loss needs a local-only assignment, which the receipts support (origin decided index 0 at resolution in the Superseded cases and the new leader's decided values `22` only).

The documented arm does win at tick periods at or below the round trip (2 ms and 4 ms both held), so the code does report Superseded for this interleaving under some schedules; the defect is that the schedule, not the durable outcome, selects the signal.
The `Superseded` arm does not confirm the caller's entry either; it stops waiting. The two arms differ in what they claim.
The band 2/4/8/16/40/80 ms was measured for one round trip (egress 1 ms each way); the threshold scales with the round trip and was not varied.
limitations: In-process in-memory transport, no crash or restart: the origin is re-synchronized from the new leader, not recovered from storage, so nothing here extends to the persistence/fail-recovery path.

One cluster shape and one fault pattern (both directions of the old leader's links dropped, election-timeout takeover, batch_size 1, majority quorum, the second entry appended through the new leader). Follower-origin assignments, batching above 1 and flexible quorums are unmeasured.

The band is characterised on one round trip only; larger egress delays or slower transports were not exercised, so the account states the relation qualitatively (tick period above the re-synchronisation round trip) with the measured points as evidence.

scope.description: Four runs of one cluster shape with real `OmniPaxos` instances driven directly through the public API in a single process (lossless in-process delivery, one entry appended on the elected leader and decided by every configured server, then trim(None) and trim(Some(decided_idx_before_trim)) on that leader). Case A is the control {1,2,3} where the largest id equals the node count; case B is the sparse {1,2,5}; case C is {2,3,4}, where the largest id exceeds the node count and id 1 is absent; case D is the two-node {1,3}, where the largest id exceeds the node count. Node ids differ only in these sets; the preferred leader is the first id of each set.
assumptions: Node ids need not be contiguous or start at 1: `ClusterConfig::validate` requires only more than one node, a non-zero configuration id, a valid quorum and that the node set contains this server's pid.
In-process lossless delivery on top of real MemoryStorage preserves the properties needed for trimming: every configured server decides the entry before the trim calls.
The first id of each set carries leader_priority 1, so elections are deterministic and only the id set differs between cases.
The leader's own accepted index and its peers' reported accepted indexes are the only inputs to the trim guard in these runs; no compaction error is injected.
excluded: Any claim about snapshot-based compaction (`snapshot` is not called).
Any claim about clusters larger than four nodes or id sets beyond these four.
Any safety claim: this probe measures progress/availability of trimming, not log consistency.

experiment.prefix: For each case: build one `OmniPaxos<TestEntry, MemoryStorage<TestEntry>>` per node id (configuration_id 1, election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, the first id carrying leader_priority 1), keep them in a pid-keyed map, and elect the first id by calling `try_become_leader()` on it and pumping (each pump: `tick()` every instance, then take_outgoing_messages and deliver each message to its receiver's `handle_incoming`) until the second id reports `get_current_leader()` as that first id with accepted=true. Emit the admission event with mode, node list and elected leader. Then append one entry on the leader and pump until every configured server reports `get_decided_idx() >= 1`; sample the leader's decided and compacted indexes; call `trim(None)`; sample the compacted index and report whether it advanced; then call `trim(Some(decided_idx_before_trim))`, sample the compacted index and report the call's result and whether it advanced. Emit the outcome under the mode-specific event name with the node list, leader, decided index, both trim results and both compaction outcomes.
semantic_changes: Two cases added for the generalised trigger and the harness parameterised on the first configured id; existing cases, measurements and comparisons unchanged.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs are produced by the target: `LeaderState::with` allocates `accepted_indexes` for every id up to the largest id in the configuration, `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` reduces over that whole vector (so phantom slots, which are never written, pin it to 0), and `SequencePaxos::trim` compares the caller's index against that value before calling `InternalStorage::try_trim`, which no-ops when the target does not exceed the current compacted index. The caller only supplies the optional trim index.

comparisons.description: Control: largest id equals the node count, trim(None) advances the compacted index.
Ids {2,3,4} with id 1 absent: predicted violated.

experiment.revision_reason: Added two cases that exercise the generalised trigger and parameterised the harness on the first configured node instead of assuming node 1 leads and is present: case C uses ids {2,3,4} (largest id 4 with three nodes, and id 1 absent from the configuration) and case D uses the two-node configuration {1,3} (largest id 3 with two nodes). Cases A {1,2,3} and B {1,2,5}, their scenario, their measurements and their comparisons are unchanged; two comparisons were added for the new cases under the same predicate.
